annotationRationale: Prime exponents exclude primes and 4. Prime/composite structure proves that n divides (n-1)! for the remaining inputs, while counting permutations by their underlying groupings proves the other factorial quotient is integral.
sourceMethod: Follows the official exclusions and its factorization into a grouping count times n!/n². The composite cases and the exact multiplicity in the grouping count are explained explicitly.

review.mathCheck: For prime \(p\), the numerator has \(p-1\) factors of \(p\), versus \(p\) in the denominator; 4 fails by exponents 11 versus 12 of 2. For every composite \(n>4\), the factor-pair argument proves \(n\mid(n-1)!\), and the unordered-group count makes the other factor integral. Including 1 leaves \(50-15-1=34\), choice D.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, independently worded adaptation of official solution 25 on pages 14 and 15. It preserves both integrality factors and expands the grouping multiplicity argument. The prime-divisor split correctly covers all composite cases.
review.annotationCheck: All cases, including 1, prime squares, 4, and the inclusive endpoints, are handled. The permutation-to-grouping explanation justifies the factorial quotient without requiring an unexplained counting formula.
